## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
7	> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
8	>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
10	>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
11	>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
12	>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
13	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
14	>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
15	>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.
16	
17	## Project Overview
18	
19	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
20	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
21	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
22	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
23	- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
24	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
25	- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
26	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
27	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
28	- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.
29	
30	## Build and Development Commands
31	
32	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
33	
34	```bash
35	# Development (fastest)
36	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
37	go run .
38	
39	# Build
40	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
41	mise run run          # Build and run
42	
43	# Testing
44	mise run test         # Run all tests
45	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
46	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
47	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
48	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
49	
50	# Code Quality
51	mise run fmt          # Format code
52	mise run vet          # Run go vet
53	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
54	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
55	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
56	mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR
57	
58	# Installation
59	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
60	```
61	
62	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
63	
64	## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules
65	
66	- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
67	- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
68	- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
69	- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
70	- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
71	- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.
72	
73	## Releases
74	
75	Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.
76	
77	## Architecture
78	
79	The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
80	**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
81	the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
82	touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

88	| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
89	| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |

96	| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |

124	### Credentials Management
125	
126	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
127	implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
128	writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
129	the credential manager *and* in plaintext:
130	
131	| Storage | Backend | Notes |
132	|---------|---------|-------|
133	| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
134	| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
135	| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |
136	
137	`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
138	The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
139	context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
140	pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
141	to the other one.
142	
143	The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
144	`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
145	second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
146	first one holds.
147	
148	`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
149	`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
150	is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
151	the auth view.

153	## Testing
154	
155	Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
156	- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
157	- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests
158	
159	Use table-driven tests where appropriate.
160	
161	**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
162	only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
163	(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
164	run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.
165	
166	**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
167	`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
168	the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
169	it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
170	writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
171	`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
172	`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
173	(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
174	tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
175	`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
176	`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.
177	
178	**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
179	port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
180	the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
181	`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
182	runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
183	(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
184	D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).
185	
186	- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
187	  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
188	  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
189	  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
190	- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
191	  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
192	- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
193	  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
194	- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
195	  enforces it yet.
196	
197	**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
198	in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
199	`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
200	versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
201	`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
202	Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
203	Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.
204	
205	**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
206	issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
207	variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
208	guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
209	`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
210	`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
211	`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
212	change an exact argv.
213	
214	**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
215	`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
216	Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
217	reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
218	`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
219	`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
220	`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call

225	`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
226	runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
227	name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
228	unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
229	`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".
230	
231	**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
232	`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. With it, `timeout` is how long the command may run in the background (default 1800000, max 7200000); at that limit it is stopped and you are re-invoked. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

description.description:

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

## Reference

    locate  ->  entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "..."
    impact  ->  entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X   (one shot: callers, callees, type consumers, data flow, co-change, siblings)
    callers ->  entire graph neighbors --repo . --symbol X --relation CALLS --direction in
    change  ->  entire graph diff --base A --head B --json
    detect  ->  entire graph capabilities --json   (inventory-only languages have no relations)
    stats   ->  entire graph stats --repo .        (human-facing token-savings report; not part of your workflow — do not run it unless asked)

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

# Planning Rules

## Implementation Plans

- **Location**: Always write implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` in the current project directory.
- **Format**: Use Markdown format for plans.
- **Naming**: Use descriptive names like `feature-name-plan.md` or `YYYY-MM-DD-feature-name.md`.

## Antigravity IDE Integration

When using the Antigravity IDE extension:
- Save all implementation plans to `.claude/plans/` relative to the project root.
- Create the directory if it doesn't exist before saving plans.
- Plans should be accessible from both Claude Code CLI and Antigravity IDE.

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	
5	> [!IMPORTANT]
6	> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
7	> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
8	>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
9	> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
10	>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
11	>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
12	>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
13	> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
14	>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
15	>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.
16	
17	## Project Overview
18	
19	DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
20	- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
21	- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
22	- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
23	- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
24	- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
25	- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
26	- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
27	- Local workspaces management with git metadata
28	- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.
29	
30	## Build and Development Commands
31	
32	Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.
33	
34	```bash
35	# Development (fastest)
36	mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
37	go run .
38	
39	# Build
40	mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
41	mise run run          # Build and run
42	
43	# Testing
44	mise run test         # Run all tests
45	mise run cover        # Coverage per package
46	go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
47	go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
48	mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)
49	
50	# Code Quality
51	mise run fmt          # Format code
52	mise run vet          # Run go vet
53	mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
54	mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
55	mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
56	mise run ci           # the six checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. CI itself runs only fmt-check, vet, lint and build: tests are disabled in CI (maintainer decision, D149), so run this locally before every PR
57	
58	# Installation
59	mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
60	```
61	
62	`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.
63	
64	## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules
65	
66	- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
67	- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
68	- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
69	- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
70	- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
71	- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.
72	
73	## Releases
74	
75	Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.
76	
77	## Architecture
78	
79	The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
80	**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
81	the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
82	touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.
83	
84	| File | Covers |
85	|---|---|
86	| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
87	| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
88	| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
89	| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
90	| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
91	| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |
92	| [`scanning.md`](../docs/architecture/scanning.md) | Trivy, Gitleaks, plumber, `scan.Categorize`, the `:sec` inventory, the two scan caches, image signatures (`internal/trust`, the cosign verifier) |
93	| [`registries.md`](../docs/architecture/registries.md) | the registry/group model and the discovered-members cache |
94	| [`network.md`](../docs/architecture/network.md) | `internal/docker` and `internal/oci` (typed `StatusError`, `...Context` variants), `internal/netproxy` (the proxy entry point every HTTP and TLS connection goes through, and its guard test, DEVDESK-581), the proxy passed to scanner containers (`netproxy.Forward`, `scan.containerRun.cmd`, the `TestContainerGuard*` guard, DEVDESK-583), `internal/imagesearch` and the registry browser's image search level, image updates (`internal/imageupdate`, the Update column), verified pulls (`internal/imagepull`), the netdiag view, `internal/ports`, `internal/netiface`, `internal/nettrace` (the path trace: unprivileged UDP + `IP_RECVERR` on Linux, ICMP echo through `iphlpapi` on native Windows) |
95	| [`mcp.md`](../docs/architecture/mcp.md) | the MCP server the TUI serves over HTTP |
96	| [`templates.md`](../docs/architecture/templates.md) | `internal/template` + `internal/ui/templates` — the repository-template catalog, its three sources, how files are fetched, and the `:templates` view |
97	| [`ui-components.md`](../docs/architecture/ui-components.md) | `components.FooterMessage`, `internal/ui/datatable`, and the activity indicator column (`internal/ui/indicator`, `datatable.IndicatorColumn`, the row sentences `components.DescribeRow`) |
98	| [`agent-usage.md`](../docs/architecture/agent-usage.md) | `internal/agentusage` — per-agent token counts from Claude Code transcripts: format, aggregation rules, tolerance, privacy (`cwd` amendment), caps, ccusage cross-check; `ListSessions`; incremental reading (`ReadDelta`, `Aggregate`, `Activity.Settled`); tool calls and time span per agent (DEVDESK-46); per-model tokens, `Billed`, and the cost estimate (`internal/agentusage/pricing`, prices from `agent_usage.prices`, DEVDESK-47); the `:agent-usage` view and its agents level and State/Tools/Duration/Est. cost columns; the Breakdown column and tab, `Usage.Categories`/`ModelTotals` (DEVDESK-98) (`internal/ui/agentusageview`) |
99	| [`nexus-bench.md`](../docs/architecture/nexus-bench.md) | `internal/nexusbench` — the disposable Nexus Community bench on the k0s cluster (DEVDESK-504, NX-01; seed, DEVDESK-505; `cut-upstream`, `restore-upstream` and `reset`, DEVDESK-534; recorded fixtures `internal/nexusfixture` (campaigns `catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) and `nexus-bench record`, DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580): decisions, the `NEXUS_BENCH_*` parameters and their validation, manifests, preflight, deployment, provisioning, destruction, the `nexus-bench` command (`cmd/nexus-bench`) and its `mise run nexus-bench:*` tasks, the upstream cut, restore and reset, the recorded fixtures (format, redaction, the `fakenexus` replay server, `record`, the stale test), what is still to come (NX-03 onward); a development tool outside `mise run ci` |
100	
101	### Status Monitoring System
102	
103	**Factory Pattern for Checkers:**
104	- `internal/status/checker.go` - Main orchestrator
105	- `internal/status/http_checker.go` - HTTP/HTTPS checks
106	- `internal/status/icmp_checker.go` - ICMP ping checks
107	- `internal/status/dns_checker.go` - DNS resolution checks
108	
109	Each checker implements `CheckerInterface`. The main `Checker.CheckOne()` uses a factory pattern to instantiate the right checker based on `component.Type`.
110	
111	**Parallel Execution:**
112	- `CheckAll()` runs all component checks concurrently using goroutines and sync.WaitGroup
113	- Results are collected and returned as `[]ComponentStatus`
114	
115	### Component CRUD Operations
116	
117	Status view supports adding/editing/deleting monitors:
118	- `internal/ui/status/components/component_form.go` - Form component
119	- `internal/ui/status/components/confirm_modal.go` - Confirmation dialog
120	- Changes persist to `~/.devdesk/config.yaml` via `config.Save()`
121	
122	State flags in Model: `creating`, `editing`, `confirming`, `selectedIdx`
123	
124	### Credentials Management
125	
126	No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
127	implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
128	writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
129	the credential manager *and* in plaintext:
130	
131	| Storage | Backend | Notes |
132	|---------|---------|-------|
133	| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
134	| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when the helper is not `store`, which writes plaintext. Context-aware. |
135	| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |
136	
137	`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
138	The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
139	context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
140	pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
141	to the other one.
142	
143	The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
144	`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
145	second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
146	first one holds.
147	
148	`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
149	`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
150	is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
151	the auth view.
152	
153	## Testing
154	
155	Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
156	- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
157	- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests
158	
159	Use table-driven tests where appropriate.
160	
161	**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
162	only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
163	(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
164	run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.
165	
166	**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
167	`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
168	the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
169	it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
170	writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
171	`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
172	`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
173	(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
174	tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
175	`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
176	`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.
177	
178	**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
179	port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
180	the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
181	`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
182	runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
183	(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
184	D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).
185	
186	- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
187	  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
188	  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
189	  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
190	- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
191	  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
192	- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
193	  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
194	- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
195	  enforces it yet.
196	
197	**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
198	in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
199	`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
200	versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
201	`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
202	Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
203	Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.
204	
205	**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
206	issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
207	variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
208	guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
209	`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
210	`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
211	`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
212	change an exact argv.
213	
214	**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
215	`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
216	Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
217	reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
218	`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
219	`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
220	`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
221	in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
222	`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
223	imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
224	(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
225	`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
226	runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
227	name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
228	unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
229	`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".
230	
231	**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
232	`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
233	literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
234	`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
235	panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
236	`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
237	colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
238	with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
239	hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
240	`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
241	(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
242	a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
243	and no key action fires (Rule 111).
244	
245	**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
246	`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
247	(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
248	handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
249	matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
250	`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
251	`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
252	`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.
253	
254	## Dependencies
255	
256	Go 1.27 (`go 1.27.3` in `go.mod`). Key libraries (versions as in `go.mod`):
257	- `charm.land/bubbletea/v2` (v2.1.1) - TUI framework (v2: `tea.KeyPressMsg`, `tea.PasteMsg`, `View() tea.View`)
258	- `charm.land/bubbles/v2` (v2.2.1) - Pre-built TUI components (table, textinput, viewport)
259	- `charm.land/lipgloss/v2` (v2.0.6) - Styling (no global colour profile; colours are `image/color.Color`)
260	- `github.com/charmbracelet/colorprofile` (v0.4.3) - colour profile `main.go` forces under Windows Terminal (replaces `termenv`)
261	- `github.com/NimbleMarkets/ntcharts/v2` (v2.9.0) - dashboard sparkline
262	- `github.com/charmbracelet/x/ansi` - ANSI-safe width, strip and cut
263	- `gitlab.com/gitlab-org/api/client-go` - GitLab API client
264	- `github.com/prometheus-community/pro-bing` - ICMP ping functionality (maintained fork of go-ping/ping)
265	- `github.com/google/go-github/v68` - GitHub API client (§3.6)
266	- `github.com/libp2p/go-netroute` - which interface a destination leaves by, on all three platforms (§3.44)
267	- `golang.org/x/sys` - direct (Rule 303): the socket calls of `internal/nettrace` (`IP_TTL`, `IP_RECVERR`, `recvmsg` on the error queue); `x/sys/windows` serves `iphlpapi` (the Windows path trace, `IcmpSendEcho2`)
268	- `github.com/zalando/go-keyring` - host secret manager (wincred / Keychain / Secret Service), no cgo
269	- `gopkg.in/yaml.v3` - YAML configuration
270	
271	## Code Conventions
272	
273	- Comments: **English only** (Rule 307) — existing French comments are not rewritten wholesale, but any new or edited comment is in English
274	- Commit messages: **English only** (Rule 307)
275	- UI text and logs: **English US only** (Rule 129)
276	- Bubbletea models define their own message types
277	- Use `theme` package for consistent styling (`internal/ui/theme/`)
278	- Config changes must call `config.Save()` to persist
279	- All colors defined in `theme/colors.go`, all styles in `theme/styles.go`
280	- Message naming: `[ComponentName][Action]Msg` (e.g., `ComponentFormSubmitMsg`)
281	- Context names: the rule exists twice (`config.ValidateContextName`, `contextcmd.ValidName`); change both or neither (`TestContextNameRulesAgree`). Creation refuses `-`, `new`, `list` (`config.ValidateNewContextName`); loading does not (D91)
282	
283	## Critical Bubble Tea Rules
284	
285	**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
286	- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
287	- `View()` is read-only
288	- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages
289	
290	**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:
291	- Use plain text: `theme.IconError + " error"` not `theme.StatusErrorStyle.Render(...)`
292	- Apply row styling via `table.SetStyles(theme.TableStylesForState("error"))`
293	
294	**Views render through `Render()`** (Bubble Tea v2): a top-level view implements
295	`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
296	router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep
297	`View() string`. Colours are `color.Color`; hex literals stay in `theme/colors.go`.
298	
299	**Update() case extraction**: If a case block exceeds 5 lines, extract to `handle[MessageType]()` method returning `(tea.Model, tea.Cmd)`

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

## Hard rules

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic
   dispatch, or related implementations could matter.
3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:
       entire graph impact --repo . --symbol X
4. Make the smallest complete edit and check sibling sites or contracts when the task implies them.
5. VERIFY before stopping. Run the most focused relevant test, build, or reproduction available.
   If execution is unavailable, perform a bounded source-level verification and state the limit.
6. Prefer precise queries and line ranges, but never trade resolution for fewer turns.
7. Feature-detect before relying on semantic relations:
       entire graph capabilities --json

## When NOT to use the graph

If the task already names the exact file and it is small, just read it — the graph saves tokens
by eliminating exploration; when there is nothing to explore, skip it.

# TUI — Rule index

TUI rules are split across 5 topic files:

| File | Rules | Content |
|---------|--------|---------|
| [`tui-layout.md`](tui-layout.md) | 101, 107, 108, 111, 112, 123, 124, 130, 134, 137, 138 | General layout, keybindings, viewport, tabs, shortcuts header, format descriptions, shortcuts obviousness |
| [`tui-theme.md`](tui-theme.md) | 102, 105, 115, 117, 118, 119, 127, 129 | Colors, lipgloss background, `theme.*` helpers, language |
| [`tui-forms.md`](tui-forms.md) | 103, 104, 113, 114, 120, 121, 131, 132, 133, 135, 140 | Forms, modals, focus, status icons, value cycling, WrappedInput, key assignment, invalid field |
| [`tui-tables.md`](tui-tables.md) | 106, 116, 122, 125, 136, 139 | Tables, column widths, plain-text cells + color via `Style`, filter bar, body never replaced (loading or message) |
| [`tui-behavior.md`](tui-behavior.md) | 109, 110, 126, 128 | Bubble Tea (Cmd/Update), scan cache, footer messages (three levels, one component) |

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

refuses, before any request, a realm whose scheme, host or port differ from the request that received the challenge, **when credentials are configured** (username and password both set, the condition 
under which Basic is sent); without credentials the anonymous token request goes out as before. Typed error `oci.ErrTokenRealmOffOrigin` (`token realm on another host (<host>)`, test with 
`errors.Is`), naming the realm's host only, never its userinfo, path or query; not a `StatusError`. The origin is compared as `sameOrigin` does (exact scheme and `u.Host`): `host` and `host:443` 
differ, `http` and `https` differ (refuse when in doubt, as D156). Two frozen exceptions (`realmExceptions` in `internal/oci/realm.go`, pinned by `TestRealmExceptionsAreFrozen`), one way only 
(registry to realm), https on both sides, host compared exactly with no port: Docker Hub (`registry-1.docker.io` to `auth.docker.io`) and **GitLab.com (`registry.gitlab.com` to `gitlab.com`, whose 
registry names `https://gitlab.com/jwt/auth` as its realm)**. A self-hosted GitLab registry whose realm is on the GitLab host stays refused: a per-configuration exception is a follow-up story. 
Rejected: following the realm with the credentials removed (an anonymous token is useless to an authenticated caller and would hide the refusal); an exception per configuration (follow-up). Reason: 
the `X-Forwarded-Host` probe of NX-05 shows that a Nexus behind a reverse proxy announces the host it is told, so a realm is not trustworthy by itself. Display: footer, level Error, `token realm on 
another host` (tags opened from the search, tags opened from the form, which used to be silent, and image search); verdict `failed` in the search. Other callers (`imageupdate`, signature, 
remediation) have no footer: journal and column unchanged. Amends D156 (the guards stopped at the scheme of the realm) and the pin of `TestMeasuredRealmStaysOnTheRegistryOrigin` (the frozen note 
`docs/measurements/2026-11-20-nexus-access.md` describes the code before this change and is not edited). (2) The 404 `Remote Auto Blocked` of a proxy whose upstream is cut is `failed`, temporary, 
detected on the JSON `message` with a body read up to 4 KiB (step 3). Implemented by DEVDESK-632: `registryStatusError(resp)` (`internal/oci/status_body.go`) reads the body only on a 404 and marks 
the `*oci.StatusError` (`UpstreamBlocked()`) when `errors[0].message` starts with `Remote Auto Blocked`, exact and case-sensitive; any other 404 stays `refused`, and a body read that ends on a 
deadline is a `*NoAnswerError` (`failed`), not a 404; `ManifestDigest` is a HEAD without a body, so a `Remote Auto Blocked` 404 on a manifest is never marked and stays a plain 404; the error reads 
`registry returned 404: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked, try again later`, never the body, date or duration; footer `Could not load tags: the proxy's upstream is temporarily blocked`. (3) 
The timeout message reads `no answer within 15 s` from `oci.RequestTimeout`, delay unchanged (step 4). Implemented by DEVDESK-633: `*oci.NoAnswerError` (`internal/oci/noanswer.go`) wraps only 
`context.DeadlineExceeded`, so no URL, userinfo, host or query reaches the message; it is applied to the request, token and body-read errors of the registry client, `context.Canceled` is untouched, a 
timely 502 stays a `*StatusError`, the verdict stays `failed`, and `registryFailureReason` shows it at the footer and in the journal. Only a delay that satisfies `errors.Is(context.DeadlineExceeded)` 
becomes a `NoAnswerError` (a transport "TLS handshake timeout" keeps its text); the Docker Hub client of `internal/imagesearch/hub.go` keeps its own untyped 15 s delay (out of scope). (4) Docker
